title: Capacity bookkeeping and burst-amnesty orchestrator (capacity-book + amnesty-controller)
author: Ellen Park
description:
Context: Customers running Dedicated fleets occasionally see transient throughput shortfalls when cross-tenant preemption, node reboots, or maintenance windows cause short-lived capacity loss. Existing autoscalers smooth utilization but do not account for small intermittent losses which cause conservative headroom shrinkage and result in repeated over-provisioning.

Motivation: Introduce explicit bookkeeping for short-lived capacity loss and a bounded 'amnesty' mechanism that lets tenants recover unused commit credits over a short window instead of being penalized by long-term reservation recalculation. This reduces oscillation in reserved capacity, improves throughput guarantees for tenants with bursty patterns, and lowers steady-state reserved capacity.

What this PR does: Adds two coordinated components: 1) capacity-book, a lightweight ledger that records short-lived capacity deltas (node drains, preempt events, maintenance) and attributes lost capacity to clusters/pools; and 2) amnesty-controller, a bounded forgiveness policy that reconciles per-tenant commit valuations when the capacity-book indicates loss was transient and within configured thresholds. The controller can proactively issue ephemeral credits or relax reservation enforcement to avoid hard reservation churn. The change is fully feature-flagged behind "capacity_book_amnesty_v1".

Design notes: - Capacity-book is implemented as an append-only time-windowed ledger (TTL 10m by default) that exposes summarized loss histograms to autoscaler components. It intentionally avoids strong consistency — eventual aggregation is sufficient for amortized decisions. - Amnesty-controller consumes the loss histogram and a tenant's recent commit history; it applies a decayed forgiveness function (alpha=0.6 default) to convert lost tokens into temporary credits capped by a per-tenant budget. - The system maintains invariants: amended capacity never violates cluster hard-limits; amnesty credits are ephemeral and expire within 5 minutes; chargeback metrics are emitted for audit.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for ledger rollup, decay math, and safety caps. - Integration tests simulate node preemptions + tenant traffic to validate no SLA regressions. - Load test against perf-canary harness with 500 tenants to measure steady-state reserved reduction and burst success rate. Results: average reserved capacity reduced by ~6.8% across runs; 95th percentile tail recoveries improved by ~22ms for burst admissions.

Rollout plan: - Feature flag default off. - Step 1: Enable in canary clusters during a 2-week observation window (ops + QE). - Step 2: Enable for low-risk customer pools with telemetry gates. - Step 3: Gradual ramp to remaining Dedicated clusters with a global kill-switch.

Telemetry and dashboards: New metrics emitted: "capacity_book.loss_events", "capacity_book.loss_histogram", "amnesty_controller.issued_credits", "amnesty_controller.expired_credits", and audit logs for reconciliation decisions. Added Grafana panels under Dedicated -> Capacity Book and a set of SLO checks to detect accidental over-admission.

Backward compatibility: All API surfaces are internal; no public API changes. Configuration knobs added to Dedicated config (defaults preserved).

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Perf canary run completed - [x] Docs stubbed in /docs/dedicated/capacity-book.md - [x] Release notes drafted

References: Linear ENG-1782, ENG-1799; related older work: ENG-903210 (hedged-autoscaler) and pr-421314 (latency-indexed-provisioner) for telemetry patterns.

Notes: This approach is intentionally conservative — amnesty only reduces churn for short transient blips. Long outages still trigger normal reservation reconciliation and customer notifications.
